rationale: With a few minutes left I built the harness the paused question asked for and ran it locally. The first version was self-throttling - it waited for each apply's future, so the FSM never fell behind - and after removing that wait the slow-FSM trial showed the effect but at a magnitude far smaller than my source-only part-answer implied: the probe was answered in a few milliseconds while the apply backlog sat behind it, because the main loop resumes as soon as one batch is accepted by the FSM, so the loop is starved per batch rather than for the whole backlog. That is a narrowing of what I recorded, and it rests on native feedback, so the harness goes in as a retained experiment with its scope stating exactly what it drives, and the question carries the corrected reading for whoever interprets the receipt.

investigations.hypothesis: The blocking send starves the main loop one batch at a time: the loop resumes as soon as the FSM accepts a batch, so the delay a caller observes is bounded by the FSM's Apply latency per batch rather than by how far the FSM has fallen behind, and a large backlog shows up as commit lag rather than as a long single stall.
investigations.discriminator: Drive a flood of applies without waiting for their futures, so the FSM falls behind, and measure a call the main loop must answer (VerifyLeader, answered inside the loop for a single voter) against an idle baseline and against a fast-FSM control; record the apply backlog at the probe, the probe latency and the probe's outcome. A probe latency on the order of the FSM's per-Apply delay with a fast control at zero supports the per-batch reading; a latency proportional to the backlog would support the stronger reading.

scope.description: Two trials on single-voter clusters. In the slow trial the FSM sleeps 25ms inside every Apply and the harness fires 400 applies without waiting for their futures, so the FSM falls behind; in the control the FSM applies without sleeping and is flooded the same way through the same code. 150ms into the flood, each trial issues VerifyLeader - answered inside the main loop for a single voter - and records its latency against an idle baseline taken before the flood, together with the apply backlog at that moment.
assumptions: A single-voter cluster is used so that no election intervenes; the leader appends and commits on its own and the FSM channel is the only queue in the picture.
VerifyLeader is a main-loop probe because verifyLeader responds inside the loop when the quorum is one, so an unresolved future means the loop is blocked.

Applies are fired without waiting for their futures, which is what lets the FSM fall behind; the first version of the harness waited and therefore measured nothing, and that correction is part of this basis.
The dry run is native feedback only; the retained execution is what an interpretation would rest on.
excluded: No application read is served and no disk or network is involved.
Only two FSM speeds are contrasted; the probe does not sweep Apply latency.
Multi-node clusters are excluded so that the probe's path to the main loop is unambiguous.

parameters.trials: trial 0 slow FSM (25ms per Apply), trial 1 fast control (no delay)
parameters.recorded_operands: apply_delay_ms, probe_elapsed_ms, baseline_elapsed_ms, probe_error, probe_slower_than_base, flood_applied, flood_target, index_lag_at_probe

comparisons.description: With a slow FSM the main-loop probe takes longer than the idle baseline, which is the leak of FSM latency into the main loop in its weakest observable form.
Control: with a fast FSM flooded the same way the probe stays at the baseline.

experiment.prefix: Each trial builds a single-voter cluster with the in-memory transport whose FSM sleeps for the trial's configured delay inside Apply. It records an idle baseline by timing VerifyLeader, then starts a goroutine that fires 400 applies without waiting for their futures, waits 150ms so the FSM can fall behind, times another VerifyLeader and records the backlog between the last log index and the last applied index, then drains and emits a summary event per trial with the delay, the two timings, the probe's error, the backlog and the apply count.
